t: You're near Cock Lane, a short road beside Smithfield market, a few minutes' walk from St Paul's Cathedral. In 1762 a lodging here became the scene of the Cock Lane ghost, a purported haunting that attracted mass public attention. The story centred on three people: William Kent, a usurer from Norfolk; Richard Parsons, a parish clerk; and Parsons' daughter Elizabeth. Elizabeth, who lived from 1749 to 1807, is remembered as the impostor behind it. It's a reminder that Londoners in the eighteenth century were just as gripped by a good ghost story as anyone today.
